internal_silent._description: Structural wrappers, literals and type-tree internals that correctly emit nothing in this lane's contract.

_groups.why: A literal/token publishes nothing by construction. The builtin-type spellings (int, string, bool, ...) are LITERAL node types in this grammar: a type POSITION is a simple_type -> long_identifier -> identifier chain, so the analyzer's BUILTIN_TYPE table (real-fsharp-analyzer.ts:3545) classifies the TEXT of a written type rather than emitting from these nodes.
A comment is not a declaration or a reference. line_comment and xml_doc were already silent.
Containers around conditional compilation: the ACTIVE region is walked normally and emits; the INACTIVE region is a design decision below. compiler_directive_decl is handled (macro symbols).
Units-of-measure expressions are type-level arithmetic, not declarations; a measure annotation is emitted through its TYPE_WRAPPER_NODES ancestor.

Wrappers/containers around a written type or constraint list. The name is emitted from the inner wrapper when it is outermost (TYPE_WRAPPER_NODES) or from the declaration node; the container itself is silent so one written type cannot earn two edges.

The analyzer walks THROUGH an expression to the names it contains; the expression node itself is not a target. rule/rules are match CLAUSES (2,648/834 in the 120-file draw): match_expression is the container and each rule a clause; neither is a reference. MEASURED that the mechanism still emits: `x.Foo()` on an SRTP emits calls (the srtp_call_expression contains the application_expression) and a `:? Foo` test emits a declared_type reference to Foo; record-construction labels are a ruling (design_decision).

Pattern syntax attaches names the identifier_pattern/argument_patterns walks already publish; the pattern operator tokens are labels. The TYPE in a type-check pattern is emitted by its written-type wrapper (measured).

property_accessor is the `with get()/set()` wrapper around a member's body — the member symbol is emitted from member_defn/method_or_prop_defn; MISSING is tree-sitter's error-recovery marker, which the analyzer never emits from (the universal pair audit-analyzer-grammar.ts:93 documents).

design_decision.description: The F# lane's contract, each ruling written against the measured shapes above. The oracle (deriveFsharpEdges in script/m14/differential.ts) implements THIS list, not the analyzer's current behavior; a disagreement is a lane defect, and the F5 row is where it is counted.

decisions.question: what is a scope, and what is its name?
decisions.resolution: A scope is one of the three nodes; its name is the first `identifier` or `long_identifier` child, taken AS WRITTEN (a dotted `module A.B` is the one name `A.B`). Nested scopes stack; the innermost scope is the source of file-level edges.

decisions.question: how is a type's kind decided?
decisions.resolution: record_type_defn -> class; union_type_defn / enum_type_defn -> enum (cases become enum_member symbols); interface_type_defn, or an anon_type_defn whose members are all signatures with no inherit and no concrete member, -> interface; delegate_type_defn / type_abbrev_defn -> type; [<Measure>] -> type; otherwise class. Record fields publish property symbols owned by the type.

decisions.question: is `inherit X` always an extends edge?
decisions.resolution: Yes, always. F# implements interfaces with `interface ... with` (FSD4); an `inherit` names a base class, so the four-line guess the analyzer uses today — 'the target starts with I followed by an uppercase letter, therefore implements' — is retired. A base class that happens to be named `IThing` is currently mislabelled implements and a genuine interface declaration is labelled by luck.

decisions.question: what implements what?
decisions.resolution: interface_implementation -> implements(type, the interface named by the first long_identifier/identifier inside it). object_expression (`{ new IFoo with ... }`) -> one class symbol named `new IFoo` owned by the enclosing scope AND implements(that enclosing scope, IFoo) — the C# family's anonymous-class precedent.

decisions.question: which member is an override, and against what?
decisions.resolution: The `override` token declares an override; a member inside `interface I with` does NOT (that is the type-level implements edge, FSD4). Source = `Owner.member`, target = `Base.member` where Base is the enclosing type's class_inherits_decl target; with no base in the file the target is the bare member name (unqualified). Only CONCRETE members (`method_or_prop_defn`) can carry the token; a `member_signature` never does.

decisions.question: what is a call, and who makes it?
decisions.resolution: The callee is the first NAMED child of an application_expression; its leaf is the last identifier of the callee's text (last segment for a dotted path, the `field:` child for a dot_expression). Four callee shapes occur in the corpus: long_identifier_or_op (17,243), a nested application_expression (4,740, curried), an infix_expression (1,348: `a |> f b`, callee = the infix's LAST named child), and a dot_expression (758). Source = the enclosing function/method/constructor; a local binding publishes no symbol but its body attributes to the enclosing callable; a computed property body emits no calls (C# family contract). Builtins (FSD11) are filtered. A call whose callee is not one of those shapes is NOT an edge (a lambda application `(fun x -> ..) y` names nothing).

decisions.question: method or property?
decisions.resolution: The grammar's `args:` FIELD decides: present (paren_pattern, identifier_pattern, argument_patterns, const unit) -> Method; absent -> the member's body follows the name, so Property. This replaces a scan of named children that recognised two of the four arg shapes and therefore filed 73 of the draw's 604 members under the wrong kind — and dropped their calls with them.

decisions.question: what is a construction?
decisions.resolution: Two forms: (a) the constructor-chain idiom `new() = Type(...)` inside an additional_constr_defn -> instantiates(constructor, Type); (b) an explicit `new` prefix (`prefixed_expression` whose first token is `new`, operand an application_expression) -> instantiates(enclosing callable, the type's leaf) and the inner application emits NO call. Bare application of a capitalised name stays a CALL: F# has no `new` keyword requirement, so what distinguishes a construction is the `new` token, not the capitalisation (the C# family's heuristic does not transfer).

decisions.question: what does `val X : T` publish?
decisions.resolution: A Function symbol named by its first identifier, owned by the enclosing module/type scope, marked metadata.isDeclaration — a .fsi declares the surface, and a later .fs definition is the SAME entity (the Clean `.dcl`/`.icl` merge precedent). Not yet implemented (gap FS-A3).

decisions.question: what does an import reference, and from where?
decisions.resolution: `open X` -> references(source = the innermost scope, or `Global` when the file declares none, target = X as written, dotted path kept). A module-less file must source its file-level edges from `Global`, never from the opened name itself: self-sourcing is how an import becomes unfalsifiable. `module X = Y` (module_abbrev) -> references(X, Y); the shape does not occur in the corpus draw (0 of 363,609 nodes) and is kept in the spec as a measured-dead branch.

decisions.question: which calls are filtered?
decisions.resolution: Console output (`printfn`/`printf`/`eprintf*`/`fprintf*`, `Console.Write*`, `Console.Error.*`) and the Object leaf methods (ToString, GetHashCode, Equals, GetType, ReferenceEquals). This is a name list shared with the analyzer — a transcription hazard the differential cannot catch — while every RULE around it is derived independently.

decisions.question: does a local publish anything?
decisions.resolution: No: a binding inside a function body is not a symbol; its body's calls attribute to the enclosing callable. Function vs variable: a declaration whose left side carries argument_patterns/type_arguments is a Function, else a Variable (module-level `let x = e`). Values are EXCLUDED from exports; symbols publish exports only for non-variable kinds.

decisions.status: RULED AND EMITTED (2026-10-09 — the `exports` ruling OVERTURNED)
decisions.question: what does this file PUBLISH, and is that a relationship?
decisions.resolution: The FS-D8 importable-unit set, emitted as one `exports` edge per unit (analyzer name: FS-D13; the payload channel is unchanged). TARGET = the symbol's published identity (`metadata.fqn`, the same spelling `contains` uses); SOURCE = the publishing scope's published identity, or `Global` for the file's own top-level unit, which has no owner (FS-D10's file-scope spelling — no module name is invented from the filename). Metadata: `exportForm: module-surface`, `declaredKind`, `visibility`, `publishedBy` (enclosing-scope | file-scope), `sourceResolution` (the same three-valued class `contains` writes), `targetResolution: published-identity`. THE OLD RULING IS OVERTURNED, and the correction is the point of this entry: it rested on INSTRUMENT A (no export-declaration node type exists — still true: 0 of 177 node types on a 288-file draw, and none of the six candidates), and instrument A cannot settle a surface that is expressed by ORDINARY declarations plus visibility. `script/m14/lua-ruled.ts` records that exact error as json's `exports` ruling. INSTRUMENT B, counted on the tree over a deterministic 288-file draw of the 6,619-file population (`bun .tmp-probe/fsharp-lane/fs-exports-census.mts 300`): **2,535 importable names in 245 of 288 files (85.1%)**, restricted by `access_modifier` (internal 120, private 70, public 10); all six export-declaration candidates 0. THE OVERLAP, priced and not hidden: of the 2,143 OWNED surface entries, **2,143 (100.00%)** are pairs `contains` already carries, and the remaining 392 (15.47%) are the file's own module/namespace headers, which `contains` cannot carry at all (no parent). That overlap does NOT make the label a duplicate: `contains` is MEMBERSHIP (type members, record fields, DU cases, private/internal lets) while `exports` is the IMPORTABLE-UNIT SET, and the programme's own M14 #49 invariant states the asymmetry in those words (`script/m14/run-fixtures.ts:1471` admits module-owned symbols as exports and refuses type-owned members with "membership rides Contains"). Measured effect: the firing instrument reads 10/10 with `exports:1109` on the corrected even-stride 120-file sample, against 9/10 and SILENT in a HEAD worktree with the same instrument; the incoming gate at 60 files reads 847 exports edges, **820 resolved (96.8%), 27 ambiguous, 0 unresolved**, moving the lane from `2961 resolved / 380 amb / 4871 unresolved` to `3781 / 407 / 4871`. OVERTURN AGAIN IF: a non-zero count of the six export-declaration node types (an explicit export list would supersede this rule), or a measurement showing the `exports` pairs are NOT the importable-unit set (a `.fsi`-restricted surface this per-file rule publishes beyond).

(1) `npx tsx script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane fsharp`, whole admitted population, production scope: edges 1,307,442 · resolved 549,197 · amb(decl) 385,465 · unresolved 372,780 · residual 58.0% · extFAIL 0 · bindFAIL 0 · causeFAIL 0 — artifact validation/m14/fixtures/fsharp/measurements/residual-gate-fsharp.txt. (3) The 370,867 bucketed by WHOSE project declares the target's exact spelling, against a key space built from every admitted file of every repository (11,807 dumped files, 121,369 distinct names, 181,553 distinct qualified names): measurements/fs-unresolved-same-project-split.txt, instrument validation/m14/fixtures/fsharp/fs-unresolved-same-project-split.py.
decisions.resolution: THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS REVERSED AT THE CURRENT TREE, and the two instruments disagree by more than a rounding: edges 1,307,442 vs 1,199,871 (+107,571), amb(decl) 385,465 vs 276,097 (+109,368). At the residual gate — the instrument the brief told this lane to start with — ambiguity EXCEEDS unresolved (385,465 > 372,780), so 'the dominant question is not collisions' does not hold for that instrument. `contains` is settled and confirms the brief's note: after fa2dc27e8 it reads 208,677 edges / 208,668 resolved / 0 ambiguous / 9 unresolved, residual 0.0%. CAUSE #1, NAMED AND COUNTED: THE EXTERNAL LIBRARY SURFACE. Of the 370,867 unresolved, by whose project declares the target: cross-project-exact 201,618 (54.4%) · in-corpus-owner 84,857 (22.9%) · nowhere-in-corpus 60,836 (16.4%) · in-corpus-leaf-only 14,507 (3.9%) · SAME-PROJECT-EXACT 9,049 (2.4%). The top targets are FSharp.Core, xUnit and FsUnit vocabulary — cross-project-exact is led by should 14,390 · Fact 11,655 · Some 8,013 · Test 5,974 · Extension 5,733 · not 5,449 · ignore 4,613 · shouldEqual 4,080 · Seq.map 3,790 · List.map 3,694, and nowhere-in-corpus by Theory 3,061 · InlineData 1,996 · System.Threading.Tasks 1,424 · Does.Contain 595. They are 'in corpus' at all only because the corpus CONTAINS THE COMPILER: `fsharp` is 6,626 of the 11,807 dumped files and ships FSharp.Core's own sources and its test idioms, so `ignore`, `Some`, `Seq.map` and `shouldEqual` are declared somewhere in the union of 26 projects. For Argu, Grace, Paket, Deedle or Fantomas they are OUTSIDE the project, and production resolves PER PROJECT. RULING: LEGITIMATE — instrument scope, not a defect. 286,475 of 370,867 (77.3%) sit in the two 'declared somewhere else' buckets and 347,311 (93.7%) name something the edge's own project does not declare; an edge inside project P naming a declaration P does not publish is correctly unresolved for that edge. Same shape as LUA-G6 in the lua lane, at 2.7x the share. NO EXTERNAL MARKER IS EMITTED AND THAT IS THE LANE'S OWN MEASURED DECISION: FS-P8 shipped one and was RETIRED 2026-10-09 after the blanket rule measured 28.0% verified / 72% refuted, and a bare identifier target has no owner for the gate's owner-lookup, so the claim would land in `ext?` (unverified) and block a pass without reducing the column. THE ACTIONABLE REMAINDER IS same-project-exact, 9,049 edges (2.4%): calls 5,615 · uses 1,619 · references 1,227 · imports 377 · implements 156 · extends 28 · instantiates 14 · contains 9 · overrides 2 · exports 2; by the analyzer's own resolution class bare-external 4,068 · external-type-or-module 2,103 · external-type 1,034 · external-namespace 754 · receiver-value 479 · local-binding 363 · module-member 120 · call-chain-receiver 121 · published-identity 11 · base-member-external 2. TWO SHAPES IN IT ARE ALREADY VISIBLY WRONG and are named for the next pass: `published-identity` 11 (`contains JS.this`, `exports Module.this`, `contains new T.this` — a member identity whose final segment is the keyword `this`), and `local-binding` 363, which is the class real-fsharp-analyzer.md §19.3 prices: the fix requires the target spelling `<callable>#<binding>` because `verifyBindingClaim` REFUTES a marked edge whose target carries no separator, and it is DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN because the differential's oracle (script/m14/fsharp-truth-oracle.ts) derives the bare spelling and is outside this lane's write scope — taking it would convert this lane's own differential rows into MISSING-plus-fabrication.
decisions.falsifier: The bucketing rests on one membership test — is the target's exact spelling declared in the edge's OWN repository — and the instrument asserts the test can answer BOTH ways before it prints: a name the compiler repo really declares IS in its set, a fabricated name is in NO repo's set, and a BCL name carried only by the compiler repo (`should`) is NOT declared by `Argu`. All three hold (CONTROL PASSES, in the artifact); had any failed the split refuses to report. If a later run shows same-project-exact growing far beyond 2.4%, this ruling is REFUTED and the external-surface reading becomes the wrong one.

decisions.decision: A record CONSTRUCTION label (`{ A = 1 }`) and a record PATTERN label (`| { A = a } |`) are NOT reference edges. The label names a member of the record type; for a type from another assembly that is a SYSTEM member no project declares, so a references edge would carry a target nothing can ever resolve, and the field's own declaration already carries its contains edge. MEASURED in the 120-file draw (validation/m14/results/fsharp-shape-census.json): named_field 376, named_field_pattern 249, field_pattern 11, record_pattern 6. Reopen only if a corpus case names a PROJECT-declared record.

Primary-constructor arguments are PARAMETERS, and this lane publishes no parameters (symbol contract: NO locals, NO lambda params, NO synthetic members). 107 occurrences in the 120-file draw. A contains edge would publish a symbol the store's symbol contract forbids; the type's contains edges are its members.

Code inside an INACTIVE preprocessor region emits NOTHING: the compiler does not see it, so a symbol or edge from it would be a fact about a program that is not being built — the same class as FS-A4's dead branches. 24 occurrences in the 120-file draw. The ACTIVE region is walked normally; the preproc_* containers are silent above.

An interpolation HOLE is not a declaration reference: the captured value is a runtime value mention, not a call, type or module reference, and this lane's calls/references come from application_expression and written type nodes — a hole has no callee and no written type. 90 occurrences in the 120-file draw.

Extern (P/Invoke and signature-file extern) declarations are NOT published: this lane's symbol contract mirrors the C# family (types, members, functions, variables, namespaces, modules) and an extern binding is a runtime import with no body. 0 occurrences in the 120-file draw — if a corpus case appears this decision reopens rather than staying a silent absence.

label_coverage._description: Which relationship labels this lane actually COMPARES, and which admitted labels have no oracle behind them. Measured by script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts and script/m14/verify-truth-existence.ts.

declared_gaps.label: contains
declared_gaps.reason: An oracle EXISTS (script/m14/oracles/fsharp-contains.ts) and is deliberately NOT wired. Measured on a 40-file fsharp draw it derives 1,178 truth rows of which 1,021 agree (86.7%), leaving 1,563 analyzer rows with no truth and 157 truth rows the analyzer does not publish. Admitting the label with that oracle would replace "not compared" with "compared against an oracle wrong in both directions", which is strictly less honest — the erlang and dart oracles were only wired after reaching ZERO disagreement in both directions. The known misses are members of `type ... as this` classes and of .fsi signature files, and a `let` with a return-type annotation whose name extraction falls through to raw node text.
declared_gaps.closes_when: the oracle reaches zero analyzer-only and truth-only rows, then wire it with its allowlist entry

declared_gaps.label: exports
declared_gaps.reason: FS-D13 (2026-10-09) OVERTURNED the old ruling, so the label FIRES — 1109 edges on the corrected even-stride 120-file firing sample, 847 on the 60-file incoming stride — and this is an EMITTED-but-UNAUDITED declaration, not the 'admitted and compared' one that stood in `declared_no_truth`. That text was false in both directions: `script/m14/differential.ts` does not admit `exports` for this lane (its fsharp expression is the base four plus `calls`, `references` and `contains`), and nothing derived truth for the label. `npx tsx script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts` reads fsharp `5471 | 5018` with `exports (85), imports (265), uses (188)` unaudited on its 25-file sample. Closes when an `exports` oracle exists in `script/m14/fsharp-truth-oracle.ts` AND the label is admitted on its own physical line in the differential's fsharp expression — the pair, in that order, because admitting without truth converts these rows into unexplained fabrications.
declared_gaps.closes_when: an exports oracle exists for this language AND the differential's allowlist admits the label; then the two readings meet

_closed.label: imports
_closed.was: `imports` is admitted for this lane and compared, but no imports oracle exists behind it, so its rows enter the comparison with no truth to meet and are counted as unexplained FABRICATIONS. That number accuses the analyzer of inventing edges when the real gap is that nobody wrote down what it should have produced — and WHICH labels surface depends on the file draw, so this list is the lane's full admitted set rather than the one a single sweep happened to hit. Closes when a imports oracle exists for this language.
_closed.now: The oracle exists and is compared. `script/m14/fsharp-truth-oracle.ts` derives `imports` from the language's three import forms: `import_decl` (`open X` / `open type X` — the same node for both spellings; the target is the written module path VERBATIM, because the leaf rule that governs every other label in this lane does not apply to a module, whose leaf is not the module), `module_abbrev` (`module X = Y` — the RIGHT-hand path; the left-hand name is the alias this very file introduces, and naming it makes every alias a self-dependency), and `fsi_directive_decl` with keyword `#r`/`#load`/`#I` (target = the specifier's string CONTENT; the node's other three keywords are REPL controls that name nothing outside the file, so the keyword is read off the tree rather than the node type being trusted). `imports` was admitted to this lane's compared set in `script/m14/differential.ts`, on its own physical line and with the stale reason that kept it out REWRITTEN rather than left beside it. Measured, not asserted: `verify-label-coverage.ts` reads fsharp `5386 | 5386` with an EMPTY un-audited column — it read `4933 | 4933` with `imports (265), uses (188)` before, and 5386 - 4933 = 453 = 265 + 188 exactly, so the movement is the two labels and nothing else; `script/m60/rel-type-coverage-gate.ts` now prints NO fsharp row in CHECK 1 and no `DERIVATION|fsharp|` line; and the differential reads 99.9% covered with neither label in `unexplained-by-label` on two draws (60 files: MISSING 3, unexplained 66, calls=65 references=1; 200 files: MISSING 15, unexplained 234, calls=231 references=3 — every residual row in another label). The check is LIVE rather than decorative, which is the part worth keeping: disabling the arm alone makes the harness's own guard fire — `COMPARED WITH NO TRUTH: imports (115 comparable, 0 truth), uses (44 comparable, 0 truth)` — and on that draw 159 of the 214 `unexplained` rows ARE these two labels (115 + 44) — with no truth behind them every comparable edge of the label is counted as a fabrication, which is the size of the population the audit covers on 60 files. The two clean readings are 66 (60 files, `calls=65 references=1`) and 234 (200 files, `calls=231 references=3`), and no before/after DELTA on one draw is claimed: the cold pool advances between runs, so the mutated and clean readings are different file sets by construction, and the claim is the population and the guard rather than a difference. NOT claimed: that the arms agree on constructs the draw did not contain (a nested `module A.B = C` path, a verbatim specifier containing a doubled quote — of which no corpus specifier has one, measured over all 193 directive nodes). The guard is a HARD FAILURE rather than a warning: a second mutated draw reads `imports (190 comparable, 0 truth), uses (74 comparable, 0 truth)` with `unexplained=335 (6.5%)` — 264 of them these two labels' whole comparable population — and the harness EXITS 6, while the clean run of the same command exits 0.

_closed.now: The oracle exists and is compared. `script/m14/fsharp-truth-oracle.ts` derives `uses` from `attribute`, which is the one F# construct a `uses` edge is FOR: it NAMES a type, applies it as a marker and never invokes it, so it is not a call (no application), not a reference (no written annotation), not a base, not an implementation and not a construction. The target is the attribute type's LEAST segment (`[<Xunit.Fact>]` names `Fact`, which is the spelling a consumer binds by) EXCEPT where this file declares a symbol under that name, when the target is that declaration's qualified name, because the written name is then provably the file's own identity rather than a same-named type from elsewhere. Two refusals are stated as rules rather than left to the read: the `target` FIELD is skipped (`[<return: Struct>]` attaches the attribute to the return, and reading the keyword as the dependency cost 11 edges in a 200-file draw), and an attribute's ARGUMENT is never read (`[<Obsolete("x")>]` names `Obsolete` and nothing inside `"x"`). Admitted to the compared set beside `imports`, with the same measurement behind it (`5386 | 5386` un-audited-empty; no fsharp row in the coverage gate; neither label in `unexplained-by-label` across two draws; and the COMPARED-WITH-NO-TRUTH guard firing at 44 comparable `uses` edges when the arm is disabled).

THE PINNED GRAMMAR DECLARES `attribute`, `attributes`, `type_attribute` and `type_attributes`, so the construct is IN the grammar; the reason is that AN F# ATTRIBUTE IS PASSIVE METADATA and a decorator is an APPLIED CALLABLE (src/ast/types.ts:131-144 — the direction is the decorated declaration → the decorator, and NOT `calls`, NOT `references`), so a `decorates` row for an F# attribute would assert an application the vocabulary does not credit. THIS IS THE CSHARP LANE'S OWN TEST, APPLIED TO F# (script/m14/spec/csharp-completeness.json — a C# attribute is PASSIVE METADATA, so the row would assert an application the vocabulary does not credit), and F#'s attributes are the same shape of thing: F#'s own [<AttributeUsage>] is literally a declaration ABOUT attributes. THE NEAR-MISS CENSUS, OVER THE WHOLE ADMITTED POPULATION (11,807 admitted files, 26 repositories — not a stride and not a sample): 68,057 attribute sites; 25,101 of them attached to a declaration (the owner by node type: `declaration_expression` 34,019, `member_defn` 12,576, `type_definition` 10,671, `union_type_case` 1,103, `module_defn` 1,807, `record_field` 863, `module_val_declaration` 1,374, `type_extension_elements` 137, `property_accessor` 160, `exception_definition` 35, `named_module` 368, `preproc_if` 70, `ERROR` 121); and 19,275 of them carry an argument. THE CSHARP LANE'S OWN QUESTION, MEASURED FOR F#: 185 of the 19,275 arguments DO carry a call somewhere inside them (`nameof …`, `defaultof<…>`), and NONE of those 185 calls the attribute's OWN TYPE — a call inside an argument list is a value the runtime evaluates, not the attribute being applied. THE GRAMMAR-SIDE HALF IS ALSO MEASURED AND IT IS NOT THE BASIS: the SERVED build's inventory (213 named types over 544 ids, sha256 16cb8779…) carries 0 decorator-application node types, and so does the newest PUBLISHED pack (200 named types, 365 in all). THE F#-SIDE HALF, MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE ADMITTED POPULATION (11,807 files, 26 repositories), AND EVERY CONSTRUCT NAMED IS COUNTED: ★ THE RENDER-HOST CALLS — 300 sites in 190 files, whose callees are `Component` 140, `render` 52, `Render` 31, `Markup` 19, `html` 12, `HtmlEncode` 12, `Html` 9, `htmlEncode` 9, `htmlString` 6, `renderHtml` 6, `RenderComponent` 2 and `HtmlString` 2 — AND NOT ONE OF THEIR 300 ARGUMENTS IS A TYPE: the argument's shape is `const` 163, `long_identifier_or_op` 70, `unit` 24, `tuple_expression` 17, `paren_expression` 11, `list_expression` 9, `application_expression` 4, `brace_expression` 1, `dot_expression` 1 ⇒ 0 of 300. denominator.rule: THE DENOMINATOR IS THE LANGUAGE'S OWN EXPRESSIBLE SET, AND EVERY TYPE IS ACCOUNTED FOR: the ten canonical types are implemented, `part_of` is implemented by the R3 remedy (2026-10-22), and the other three extended types carry an admissible ruling — `mixes_in` and `renders` on grammar absence, `decorates` on the adjudicated ontology — so each of them leaves the denominator (the gate puts a grammar-absence OR a ruling-class exclusion into `gAbs`, which shrinks `applicable`). n = 14 − 3 = 11, and the gate RECOMPUTES n and refuses a declared denominator it cannot reproduce (script/m14/coverage-block-gate.ts:933-946). THE DONE CONDITION IS SEPARATE FROM THE RATIO: the lane is NOT DONE while a type is a gap, and it is not done while a ruling rests on a construct that has not been measured.
